en.title: Kitzbühel next week: steady snow, about 18 cm up high (forecast 23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Next week's fresh snow in Kitzbühel: 3–34 cm on the upper slopes and 2–14 cm at the base (23–29 November 2026), best day, best slopes and how sure the forecast is.
en.lede: After a modest start this week (10 cm at the top from 17 to 20 November), Kitzbühel lines up another round. Next week, 23 to 29 November, brings 18 cm up high in the middle of our forecast, anywhere from 3 to 34 cm, and 8 cm at the base.

sections.h: What falls where on the Kitzbühel slopes
p: Read from the top down: 18 cm near 1800 m, 18 cm near 1400 m, 8 cm near 800 m. The low-to-high spread is 3–34 cm at the top and 2–14 cm at the base.
Most of the total arrives on Friday 27 (5 cm, up to 8) and Sunday 29 (7 cm, up to 15), counted at the top as the middle of our forecast and the high case.

sections.h: The range, not just the number
p: Treat this one with caution: 3 cm at the low end, 34 cm at the high end. A spread that wide a week out means the storm may still slide away from Kitzbühel or sit right over it.
The days closest to now are the most reliable; the end of the week is the least.
Sunday 29 November brings the most, 7 cm at the top and 15 cm at best: enough to soften the pistes, not enough for a powder day.

Where to look in Kitzbühel: the Pass Thurn side, the coldest part of the area. The snow-sure top is the Resterhöhe and the Pengelstein; the part to treat with caution is the town of Kitzbühel and the lower Hahnenkamm runs.
For comparison, the upper slopes of the closest big resorts collect Saalbach (21 km away) 17 cm, Mayrhofen (51 km away) 17 cm and Hintertux (65 km away) 14 cm; Kitzbühel sits at 18 cm.
A few centimetres either way is inside the forecast's own margin, so Kitzbühel and its neighbours are effectively level.
Half-and-half at the bottom: 8 cm near 800 m is a fair amount, but well short of the top's 18 cm. Mild spells will turn the lowest runs heavy and sticky.
Kitzbühel is low for a big name, so the depth on its lower runs depends on cold nights and snow-making.
Unlike the French side of the Alps, Kitzbühel sees only 10 cm up high from 17 to 20 November (5–15 cm). So next week's snow is most of the fortnight's story here.

advice: Before leaving the pistes in Kitzbühel, check the regional avalanche service of the province.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Plan around the top's 18 cm, and keep the high case of 34 cm as a bonus.
